subject: Deployment demarcation and operational handshake for private VPC
messages:
From: Tara Bowen <tara@acmecloud.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: ops@skyline-int.com, eng-ct@acmecloud.com
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy — demarcation & egress expectations (diagram attached)

Hi Jonas / Irene —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We want to lock down the demarcation between our network boundary and Redwood's control plane for the Acme private deployment. Attached is a quick sketch from our infra team (redwood_acme_vpc_demarcation_v1.pdf) — it shows a peered VPC, a private link to a control plane endpoint, and a dedicated egress NAT for telemetry.

Key asks from Acme:
- Confirm which control plane endpoints will be public vs private (we need private endpoints for audit reasons).
- What traffic must traverse our egress vs Redwood’s managed egress (metrics, model updates, heartbeats).
- Recommended firewall rules and port ranges for the data plane agents (we prefer a minimal open surface).
- A short mutual action plan (timeline + cutover checklist) we can share with our security reviewers.

Can you confirm whether the control plane will accept connections over a private peering or whether we need an outbound proxy in our VPC? Tara + Skyline, please add any constraints we should be aware of (eg. outbound-only policy, no incoming connections allowed).

Appreciate a short summary and proposed next steps by EOD tomorrow if possible — we're trying to get the security review scheduled next week.

Thanks,
Tara Bowen
Head of Cloud Platform
Acme Cloud
(attachment: redwood_acme_vpc_demarcation_v1.pdf - diagram)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tara Bowen <tara@acmecloud.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: ops@skyline-int.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — demarcation & egress expectations (diagram attached)

Tara — thanks for the clear list and the sketch. High level answers below; I'll loop in Irene for the low-level porting and Mina/Soojin for the ops cutover.

1) Control plane endpoint model:
- Primary control plane (API, rollout coordination, metrics ingestion) can be hosted behind a private ALB in our control VPC and exposed via VPC peering / PrivateLink depending on your preference. PrivateLink is preferred if Acme enforces strict route tables and no cross-VPC routing.
- We can offer a customer-dedicated private endpoint (private DNS + mTLS) so no public ingress is required.

2) Egress responsibilities:
- Required outbound from your VPC: health-check pings to control plane, periodic KV sync (TLS over 443), and S3-compatible object pulls for model artifacts — these are outbound connections from your data plane to Redwood-managed endpoints.
- Redwood-managed egress: telemetry ingestion (metrics, traces) can be optionally proxied through Redwood if you enable a managed egress path; otherwise, data plane agents will push directly to your configured telemetry endpoints.

3) Firewall / ports (minimal set):
- Outbound TCP 443 -> control-plane-private-endpoint (TLS, mTLS optional).
- Outbound TCP 443 -> artifact storage endpoint (if using Redwood-hosted models).
- If you enable SSH-based support sessions (optional), outbound TCP 22 to a jumpbox; otherwise we use an agent with ephemeral tunneling initiated from your side.

4) Mutual action plan (draft):
- Day 0–2: Exchange network CIDR + PrivateLink requirements; Acme confirms egress policy.
- Day 3–5: Redwood provisons private endpoint; Acme configures route tables / endpoint.
- Day 6–7: Smoke test with sample model pulls + small inference job; security team validation.
- Day 8: Cutover window and rollback plan.

I'll attach a concise deploy checklist (redwood_acme_deploy-checklist.xlsx) and a pared-down diagram with recommended NAT/egress placement. Irene — could you confirm the required ports for the data-plane agent and whether our agent supports outbound-only connectivity without inbound holes?

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_acme_deploy-checklist.xlsx)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, Tara Bowen <tara@acmecloud.com>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com, ops@skyline-int.com
Date: 2027-09-18T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — demarcation & egress expectations (diagram attached)

Jonas / Tara — quick technical clarifications and a minimal port table from our infra team. Yes — our data-plane agent supports outbound-only mode; it establishes TLS sessions to the control plane and maintains a secure mTLS channel for KV cache refresh and model fetches. No inbound ports required on customer side for normal operation.

Minimal port table (customer egress rules):
- 443 outbound to control-plane-private-endpoint (TLS/mTLS) — agent & heartbeat
- 443 outbound to artifacts endpoint (if using Redwood-hosted artifacts)
- 443 outbound to telemetry endpoint(s) (if using Acme-managed telemetry)
- 123 UDP outbound (optional) for NTP if compliance requires synchronized clocks (we can accept controlled NTP via your internal ntp pool)

Notes / constraints:
- Model artifacts: large pulls may happen during first sync — recommend either a temporary increased bandwidth allowance during onboarding or pre-staging artifacts to an internal artifact store that the agent can access locally.
- Telemetry: if Acme requires telemetry to never leave your VPC, we can disable Redwood ingestion and emit metrics to a local collector instead. Some Redwood features (rolling quality alerts) rely on centralized signal ingestion — we can configure a privacy-preserving subset.
- Heartbeats: frequency is configurable; default 30s. If your egress policy is aggressive, we can increase to 60–120s to minimize connections.

Operational handoff checklist (high level) — see attached spreadsheet for full steps. Action items for Acme: provide CIDR blocks for peering/PrivateLink, confirm whether PrivateLink is required, and confirm whether telemetry must be retained in VPC. Action items for Redwood: provision dedicated private endpoint, provide TLS mTLS cert bundle, and provide runbook for cutover/rollback.

Irene Choi
Staff Engineer, Network & Infra
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deploy — demarcation & egress expectations (diagram attached)

Thanks Jonas / Irene — this is really helpful. A few follow-ups from the security review:

- Acme requires PrivateLink (no peering) for control plane connectivity due to route table restrictions.
- Telemetry must stay in our VPC for 90 days; we will accept a privacy-preserving summary to Redwood for feature flags, but raw traces/metrics must remain internal.
- We'll pre-stage the model artifacts into our S3-like internal store and provide credentials to the agent so initial syncs don't hammer your artifact buckets.

Next steps:
1) We'll provision an interface endpoint and share the endpoint ID + subnet list by EOD Monday.
2) Tara will schedule a 60-minute cutover window for next Thursday (preferred) — ops@skyline-int.com to confirm exact time.
3) Redwood: please send the mTLS cert bundle and the trimmed deploy checklist PDF variant that we can attach to our security attestation.

If you can send the cert bundle and the trimmed checklist before Monday, that will keep us on schedule. Thanks again — looking forward to the smoke test.

—Tara
Tara Bowen
Head of Cloud Platform
Acme Cloud
